layers.label: Abstraction
layers.title: Hardware Abstraction Layer
layers.description: Every motor, servo, and sensor is wrapped in a subsystem class — Intake, Spindexer, Camera, Turret — so the rest of the code never touches raw hardware. This keeps opmodes readable, makes hardware swaps a one-line change, and lets us reuse the same subsystem structure season after season without rewriting the foundation.
bullets: One subsystem class per mechanism — no raw hardware in opmodes
Hardware mapped in a single place; swaps are one-line changes
Subsystem structure carries over between seasons
Unit-testable logic separated from hardware calls

layers.label: Control
layers.title: Closed-Loop Control
layers.description: On top of the hardware layer sits the control code — PID controllers, feedforward models, and motion profiles that turn a target into smooth, repeatable motion. Whether it's holding a lift height under load or driving to an exact heading, control loops read sensor feedback continuously and correct in real time rather than guessing with open-loop timing.
bullets: PID + feedforward on every position- and velocity-critical mechanism
Motion profiling for smooth acceleration and jerk limits
Sensor feedback closes the loop — no timing-based guesses
Gains tuned live and stored per mechanism

layers.label: Autonomy
layers.title: Autonomous & Navigation
layers.description: The autonomous layer combines localization, path following, and vision correction to run repeatable routines without a driver. For DECODE we fused two odometry sources — an optical odometry sensor and a goBILDA Pinpoint computer — to track the robot's pose, drove planned paths with Pedro Pathing, and used AprilTag vision to snap the estimate back to ground truth so error never compounds across a 30-second routine.
bullets: Pose tracking fusing optical odometry and a goBILDA Pinpoint (DECODE)
Pedro Pathing for smooth Bézier-curve path following with heading control
AprilTag vision correction to eliminate accumulated drift
Routines swappable at match time based on alliance

layers.label: Tooling
layers.title: Telemetry & Tuning
layers.description: None of this is possible without visibility. We stream live telemetry to FTC Dashboard, tune PID gains and path constants without redeploying code, and log every run so a failure at competition can be replayed and diagnosed in the pit. The tooling layer is what turns a slow guess-and-check process into fast, data-driven iteration.
bullets: Live telemetry and field visualization via FTC Dashboard
Gains and constants tuned without recompiling
Every run logged for pit-side replay and diagnosis
All code version-controlled in Git across the season
